solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Eastern memorials left instead of first new profits

indicators.note: one letter stands in place of another, so left replaces the earlier of the two n's
first says only the earlier of the two n's in the memorials word is swapped

parts.note: monuments are memorials to the dead or to events

explanation.surface: Some oriental monuments have been turning a profit for their owners.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first N of the memorials word changes to L; the second N stays.
explanation.definitionFit: Emoluments are the salary, fees or other earnings someone receives from employment.

clue.text: Treasury's former auditor picked up

parts.note: ex- means former

indicators.note: heard, as by a microphone, so the auditor word is replaced by one sounding the same

parts.note: an auditor is a checker of accounts

explanation.surface: A one-time Treasury official was arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: Picked up suggests an arrest, but it signals a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: The Exchequer is the UK government department that manages public funds, the national treasury.

clue.text: Female leaves old seafood in the Channel Islands

indicators.note: the female letter departs from the old word

parts.note: former means old, previous

explanation.surface: A woman walks away from the old seafood on Jersey or Guernsey.
explanation.walkthrough: The Channel Islands are British islands off the coast of France.
explanation.definitionFit: The ormer is an edible abalone shellfish prized as a delicacy in Guernsey and Jersey.

clue.text: Student outside university arranged duet to be broadcast

indicators.note: the scrambled letters sit around the university letter
scattered widely, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: these words supply their own letters as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A student away from campus has arranged a duet for radio.
explanation.walkthrough: Arranged looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An undergraduate is a university student who has not yet taken a first degree.

clue.text: One takes off Parisian art stunt

parts.note: es is French for thou art, so a Parisian's art
a caper is a prank or stunt

explanation.surface: Someone sends up a Parisian art prank.
explanation.walkthrough: Art is the old verb form, as in thou art, not painting.
explanation.definitionFit: An escaper is someone who takes off, fleeing from captivity.

clue.text: Clean up the fourth city

indicators.note: in a down entry the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to valet a car is to clean it
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Tidy up the fourth city.
explanation.definitionFit: Tel Aviv is Israel's second-largest city, on the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: SA resident ambassador seized by gunmen

definitions.note: SA here is South America, where this flightless bird lives

indicators.note: the ambassador is held inside by the gunmen, so those letters go within

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the army's gunners
HE stands for His Excellency, the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: An envoy is taken hostage by armed men in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: SA reads as South Africa in the surface, but the bird lives in South America.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhea is a large flightless bird native to South American grasslands.

clue.text: Hit boss with iodine, stopping ache

indicators.note: the boss and iodine stop up a gap inside the ache word

parts.note: to hunger is to ache for something
MD is managing director, the boss

explanation.surface: A manager strikes, with iodine soothing the pain.
explanation.walkthrough: Hit is a noun: a smash success.
explanation.definitionFit: A humdinger is an outstanding thing, a real hit or knockout.

clue.text: Poet's article getting around hurdles at regular points

indicators.note: the article goes around the chosen letters

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: every other letter of hurdles is taken

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of hurdles are kept

explanation.surface: A poet's article on clearing hurdles at intervals.
explanation.definitionFit: W. H. Auden was an Anglo-American poet, author of Funeral Blues.

clue.text: Fellow doctor's gagging

definitions.note: an adjective here: given to telling gags

parts.note: co- is the prefix for a fellow or partner, as in co-worker
a medic is a doctor

explanation.surface: A fellow physician is choking on something.
explanation.walkthrough: Gagging suggests choking, but here it means cracking gags.
explanation.definitionFit: Something comedic is funny, full of gags or jokes.

clue.text: Enthusiastically appreciated hosting graduate

indicators.note: the appreciation word holds the graduate within it like a host with a guest

parts.note: to like something is to appreciate it
MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: A party thrown for a new graduate went down very well.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something like mad means doing it with great energy and enthusiasm, an informal idiom.

clue.text: Erudite king currently fit to put up shelf

indicators.note: in a down entry the shelf is put up, above the fit word

parts.note: now means at present, currently
a ledge is a shelf
able means fit or capable

explanation.surface: The king is now able to put up a shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: Put up is DIY in the surface, but means placed higher in the column.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone knowledgeable is well-informed and learned, as an erudite scholar is.

clue.text: Slip and panic, cutting head

indicators.note: the head, or first letter, of the panic word is cut off

parts.note: terror is extreme fear or panic

explanation.surface: A fall and a moment of panic result in a cut head.
explanation.walkthrough: Slip suggests a stumble, but it is a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip is a small mistake, an inadvertent blunder.

clue.text: Responding instinctively, I sent in sweet note

indicators.note: the letter I is dispatched into the dessert word

parts.note: a pavlova is a meringue dessert, a sweet
the letter I taken straight from the clue
N is note as abbreviation

explanation.surface: Someone reacts on impulse after sending a dessert and a message.
explanation.walkthrough: A pavlova is a meringue pudding topped with cream and fruit; Pavlov's dogs drooled at a bell.
explanation.definitionFit: Pavlovian describes a conditioned reflex, a reaction made automatically without thinking.

clue.text: Enjoying fewer rights, poor endured pig liver

indicators.note: something poor is badly made, so these letters are rearranged into a better form

parts.note: these words supply their own letters as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A deprived person has had to put up with eating pig's liver.
explanation.walkthrough: Poor wants to belong with the definition, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The underprivileged have fewer advantages and opportunities than others in society.

clue.text: Twice United merited awful "D"

definitions.note: D is the chemical symbol for this isotope

indicators.note: something awful is a mess, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: U for United, taken twice
this word supplies its own letters as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: United twice earned a terrible D grade.
explanation.walkthrough: D looks like a grade, but it is the symbol for heavy hydrogen.
explanation.definitionFit: Deuterium, heavy hydrogen, is the stable hydrogen isotope with chemical symbol D.

clue.text: Devoted daughter improved paper for university

indicators.note: the paper letter stands in for the university letter

parts.note: educated means improved through learning
the i is a British newspaper

explanation.surface: A devoted daughter improved her paper for university.
explanation.walkthrough: The i is a UK national newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Dedicated means committed or devoted to a task or cause.

clue.text: Shell ought to be red not black, curved further up

parts.note: a round is a shell or cartridge of ammunition
should means ought to

indicators.note: the black letter is taken out, leaving the rest

parts.note: the clue's own words, before the black letter is dropped
B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: A seashell ought to be red in colour, not black, with a curve at the top.
explanation.walkthrough: Shell suggests seashells, but it is artillery ammunition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone round-shouldered has a stooping posture, with the upper back hunched forward.

clue.text: Career encompasses European court area

indicators.note: the career word surrounds the European and court letters

parts.note: to career is to rush along, as does to hare

explanation.surface: A career spans a European court area.
explanation.walkthrough: Career is the verb meaning to rush, not a profession.
explanation.definitionFit: A hectare is a metric unit of area equal to ten thousand square metres.

clue.text: Work by Joyce Grant

definitions.meaning: second meaning: first name of ... S. Grant, US president

explanation.walkthrough: Grant reads as a gift of money, but is the Civil War general and president.
explanation.definitionFit: The novel by James Joyce and the forename of General Grant share the Latin name of Odysseus.

clue.text: After Henry I, archery reshaped the pecking order

indicators.note: the reshaped archery letters follow Henry and I

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: given a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: this word supplies its own letters as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: After the reign of King Henry I, archery reorganised its ranking system.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry I looks like the king; it is H and the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A hierarchy is a ranking of status, which pecking order describes idiomatically.

clue.text: Correspondents shed, first to last

indicators.note: the opening letter moves to the end

parts.note: a shack is a shed or hut

explanation.surface: Reporters shed their first letter at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: Shed looks like a verb but is the hut.
explanation.definitionFit: Hacks is a slang term for journalists, especially newspaper reporters.

clue.text: Name taken from traditional rules of behaviour

definitions.note: plural phrase for a singular answer; an ethic is a set of such rules

indicators.note: the name letter is removed from the traditional word

parts.note: ethnic can mean traditional, as in ethnic dress

explanation.surface: A name has been dropped from the traditional code of conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethic is a set of moral principles that govern how one should behave.

clue.text: Underworld spooks beheaded

indicators.note: the head, the first letter, is lopped off

parts.note: shades are ghosts, spooks

explanation.surface: Ghosts with heads cut off haunt the netherworld.
explanation.definitionFit: Hades is the Greek underworld, the realm of the dead.

clue.text: Fancy area at the back of Big Ben perhaps

indicators.note: the area letter goes behind, after the clock word

parts.note: Big Ben, the great bell in London's clock tower, is an example of something that chimes

explanation.surface: An ornate patch at the rear of London's famous clock tower.
explanation.walkthrough: Big Ben is the great bell of the Palace of Westminster clock, so a chimer.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimera is a fanciful illusion or wild fantasy of the imagination.

clue.text: Correct spades for one edging plot

indicators.note: the suit word forms an edge around the plot word

parts.note: spades is one example of a suit in cards
a bed is a garden plot

explanation.surface: Spades are used to trim the edge of a garden plot.
explanation.walkthrough: Spades suggests digging tools, but it is a card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: To subedit is to correct and prepare copy for publication, as a newspaper editor does.

clue.text: Reservoir to sketch — later you must leave

indicators.note: it is the later of the two u's that goes
the letter for you departs from the sketch phrase

parts.note: to sum up is to outline briefly, to sketch
U sounds like you, as in text speak

explanation.surface: An artist is told to draw a reservoir and then go.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the first U would leave SMUP, so the later one goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A sump is a pit or well where liquid collects, such as the oil reservoir in an engine.

clue.text: Study covers energy in ships, English, given new rating

indicators.note: the study word wraps around everything else

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university

indicators.note: the energy letter sits inside the ships letters

parts.note: SS is a steamship; two ships give two SS's

explanation.surface: A study of energy in English ships leads to a revised rating.
explanation.walkthrough: Ships is plural, so the SS for steamship appears twice.
explanation.definitionFit: To be reassessed is to be evaluated again and given a fresh rating or valuation.
